questions.q: Mrs. Adebayo bought a blender from a Lagos market. After two weeks it stopped working. She returned to the seller who refused to repair or replace it, insisting the sale was final. Which consumer right is Mrs. Adebayo primarily entitled to claim?
options: Right to redress (repair, replacement or refund) for defective goods
Right to reasonable price for goods
Right to information about goods
Right to choice among competing products
questions.explanation: The right to redress covers repair, replacement or refund when goods are defective. Reasonable price, information and choice are other consumer rights but do not directly address a faulty blender needing repair or replacement.

questions.q: Which Nigerian agency should a consumer contact if a seller is engaging in false advertising about the nutritional benefits of a packaged cereal?
options: Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC)
Nigerian Customs Service
Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) or the Consumer Protection Council (CPC)
Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS)
questions.explanation: SON and the Consumer Protection Council handle standards and misleading claims; either agency is appropriate. Customs, CAC and FIRS deal with imports/companies/taxation and are not primarily responsible for consumer false-advertising claims.

questions.q: A shop displays a price tag N3,500 on a pair of shoes but charges N4,000 at the cashier. Under consumer protection law, this practice is best described as:
options: Predatory pricing
Price fixing
Loss leader pricing
Deceptive pricing
questions.explanation: Charging more than the displayed price is deceptive pricing (misleading the consumer). Price fixing involves firms agreeing on prices; predatory pricing means pricing very low to drive out competitors; loss leader is selling below cost to attract customers. None describe charging higher than the displayed price.

questions.q: Which document is commonly used to evidence ownership and transfer of goods being transported by sea and is negotiable by endorsement?
options: Invoice
Bill of lading
Delivery note
Packing list
questions.explanation: A bill of lading is a negotiable document of title for goods carried by sea. An invoice is a commercial bill for payment, packing list details contents, and delivery note confirms receipt; none are negotiable title documents.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter sends goods to Accra and issues a sight bill of exchange for $5,000 payable on presentation. What must the importer do to settle the bill?
options: Pay the $5,000 immediately upon presentation of the bill
Refuse the bill and wait for a documentary credit
Pay only half now and half after 30 days
Accept the bill and pay after the agreed credit period
questions.explanation: A sight bill requires immediate payment when presented. Accepting and paying later applies to term bills; refusing requires negotiation but does not meet sight bill terms; splitting payment is not permitted by sight bill conditions.

questions.q: Which document from the carrier shows the condition of goods at the time of loading and often protects the exporter against claims for damaged goods in transit?
options: Pro forma invoice
Insurance policy document
Clean bill of lading (no marks or damages recorded)
Commercial invoice
questions.explanation: A clean bill of lading indicates goods were loaded in good condition, helping exporters avoid claims for pre-shipment damage. Insurance policies cover loss but don't describe loading condition; invoices document value and sale, not carriage condition.

questions.q: Tunde pays an annual premium of N12,000 for a motor policy that provides third-party liability cover. If his insurer charges an extra N3,000 to extend cover to own-damage, what will be his total premium for both covers for one year?
questions.explanation: Total premium equals base premium plus extension: N12,000 + N3,000 = N15,000. N12,000 would be only third-party cover; N9,000 is less than base and N3,000 is only the extra for own-damage.

questions.q: Which principle of insurance requires the insured to disclose all material facts about the risk to the insurer before the contract is made?
options: Utmost good faith (uberrima fidei)
Proximate cause
Contribution
Indemnity
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith obliges full disclosure of material facts. Indemnity compensates for loss, proximate cause determines cause of loss, and contribution deals with multiple insurers sharing liability; none require initial full disclosure.

questions.q: The Central Bank of Nigeria reduces bank reserve requirements. Which immediate effect is the CBN intending to achieve?
options: Higher interest rates to curb inflation
Decrease in money supply due to lower deposits
Increase in banks' ability to create loans and expand credit
Reduction in government revenue from taxes
questions.explanation: Lower reserve requirements free up funds for banks to lend, expanding credit and money creation. It does not directly decrease money supply, raise interest rates (it tends to lower them), nor affect government tax revenue directly.

questions.q: If a customer deposits N200,000 into a savings account paying 6% simple annual interest, how much interest will the customer earn in 9 months?
questions.explanation: Simple interest = principal × rate × time = 200,000 × 0.06 × (9/12) = 200,000 × 0.06 × 0.75 = 9,000. N12,000 would be for 12 months; N6,000 is for 6 months; N18,000 is for 18 months.

questions.q: Fatima runs an online boutique in Abuja. She accepts payment by card and transfers the order to a courier. Which of the following best describes the most likely legal relationship between Fatima and the courier company when the courier collects goods for delivery?
options: A partnership between Fatima and the courier to sell the goods
An insurance contract that makes the courier insurer of the goods
A contract of carriage where the courier acts as a bailee and is responsible for delivering goods safely
A sale contract transferring ownership to the courier immediately
questions.explanation: When a courier collects goods for delivery, the relationship is typically a contract of carriage and the courier acts as a bailee responsible for safe delivery. Ownership remains with the seller until conditions of sale are met, so it is not an immediate sale. It is not a partnership nor an insurance contract.

questions.q: An online seller in Lagos advertises a wristwatch for N15,000 but later refuses to deliver claiming the price was a typing error and demands N30,000. Under Nigerian consumer protection principles for electronic commerce, which is the best argument the buyer can use?
options: The buyer must pay N30,000 because advertised prices are treated as invitations to treat only
The buyer can take the seller to criminal court for fraud automatically
The buyer has no rights because online prices are always subject to correction
The seller is bound if the buyer reasonably relied on the displayed price and there was implied acceptance by completing purchase steps
questions.explanation: If a buyer reasonably relied on a clearly displayed price and completed the purchase process, the seller may be bound; it is not always merely an invitation to treat. Sellers can correct genuine mistakes in some cases, but blanket claims that online prices are always corrigible are wrong. Criminal prosecution is not automatic; civil remedies are typical.

questions.q: Chinedu wants to sell digital art on an online marketplace that hosts multiple sellers and provides payment processing. Which statement about the marketplace's likely legal status is correct?
options: The marketplace acts as a bank and must insure seller losses
The marketplace is usually considered an intermediary/platform and not the seller; liability for defective content may be limited under intermediary rules
The marketplace is always the seller and guarantees every transaction
The marketplace must hold title to all goods sold on it
questions.explanation: Online marketplaces typically act as intermediaries connecting buyers and sellers and often have limited liability under intermediary rules. They are not automatically the seller, do not hold title to all goods, and are not banks required to insure seller losses.

questions.q: Olu runs a co-operative society for market traders in Ibadan. Which of the following is a primary advantage of the cooperative form of business for these members?
options: Centralised control by a single owner who decides all operations
Limited ability for members to vote on major decisions
Unlimited personal liability of each member for society debts
Members pool resources to obtain credit at favourable rates and share profits democratically
questions.explanation: A key advantage of cooperatives is pooling resources for credit and democratic sharing of profits/decisions. Cooperatives do not impose unlimited personal liability on all members in the same way sole traders do, nor are they centrally controlled by a single owner; members generally have voting rights.

questions.q: A family company in Kano is registered as a private limited liability company with three shareholders who are all family members. Which of the following is a true legal characteristic of this company?
options: Shares of the private company must be offered to the public
Shareholders are personally liable for all company debts beyond share capital
Shareholders' liability is limited to the unpaid amount on their shares
The company cannot enter into contracts in its own name
questions.explanation: In a private limited liability company the shareholders' liability is limited to unpaid portion on their shares. They are not personally liable for company debts beyond this, the company can contract in its own name, and shares need not be offered to the public.

questions.q: A quoted company on the stock exchange declares a 5-for-1 stock split. Which effect should shareholders expect immediately after the split?
options: Each shareholder's percentage ownership in the company will be halved
Each shareholder will have five times the number of shares but market price per share will be roughly one-fifth, total value unchanged
Total market value of each holding will increase fivefold
Dividends per existing share in aggregate increase five times
questions.explanation: A stock split increases number of shares and reduces price per share proportionally so total value remains unchanged. It does not change ownership percentages nor increase total value or aggregate dividends.

questions.q: Mr. Okoro hires casual labourers on a cocoa farm in Ondo state during harvest. Which payment method would best encourage efficiency while aligning labourer pay to output?
options: Daily time rate that pays the same regardless of crates harvested
Payment only at the end of the season with no interim pay
A fixed annual salary unrelated to harvest output
Piece-rate payment where workers are paid per crate harvested
questions.explanation: Piece-rate payment ties pay to output and encourages efficiency. A time rate does not reward higher output, a fixed salary is unrelated to performance, and end-of-season-only pay may reduce motivation and present cash-flow issues.

questions.q: Which promotional method would be most effective for Musa, who wants to create immediate foot traffic to his new electronics shop in Kano during a one-week opening sale?
options: Sponsoring a state-level industry seminar next month
Running a long-term brand-building TV campaign nationwide
Publishing a detailed product catalogue to be mailed quarterly
Distribution of discount coupons redeemable only in the shop during the sale week
questions.explanation: Discount coupons redeemable in-store during the sale create urgency and drive immediate foot traffic, which fits a one-week opening sale. A long-term TV campaign and sponsoring a seminar are better for brand awareness over time, while a quarterly catalogue is slow and not timely for a week-long event.

questions.q: An advertiser claims a detergent 'removes stains 50% faster than the leading brand' without stating test conditions. Which advertising principle is being violated?
options: Price stability (advertising should not change prices)
Comparative advantage (advertiser must avoid comparisons)
Truthfulness and substantiation (claims must be supported and not misleading)
Decency (advertising must avoid offensive language)
questions.explanation: The claim lacks substantiation and could mislead consumers, so it violates truthfulness and the need to support comparative claims. Comparative advantage is allowed if supported; decency and price stability are unrelated to making unsupported performance comparisons.

questions.q: During market research, Ifeoma uses a small group of customers to discuss opinions about a new snack brand. This qualitative method is called:
options: Focus group
Observation study
Questionnaire survey
Experimental test market
questions.explanation: A focus group is a qualitative method using a small group to discuss opinions. A questionnaire survey is typically quantitative and broader, observation records behaviour without discussion, and an experimental test market manipulates variables in a real market rather than group discussion.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter sells cocoa beans to a buyer in Rotterdam under CIF terms. Which cost is the exporter responsible for paying?
options: Freight and insurance to Rotterdam port
Customs clearance at the buyer's country
Inland distribution from Rotterdam to the buyer's warehouse
Import duty payable in the Netherlands
questions.explanation: Under CIF (Cost, Insurance and Freight) the exporter pays cost of goods, freight and insurance to the named destination port. Import duty, inland distribution and import customs clearance in the buyer's country are the buyer's responsibility.

questions.q: A Lagos exporter receives a bill of lading marked 'clean on board'. This means the goods:
options: Were loaded on board the ship in apparent good condition
Are insured against all risks at sea
Have passed customs inspection in the buyer's country
Are free from import duties
questions.explanation: 'Clean on board' indicates the carrier received the goods on board without visible damage or defects at loading. It does not say anything about insurance, customs in the buyer's country, or import duties.

questions.q: If the naira weakens significantly against the US dollar, an exporter in Nigeria who invoices in dollars will most likely:
options: Lose naira on export receipts because the dollar fell
Have to pay additional export duty to the Nigerian government
Be unaffected because exchange rates do not affect exporters
Receive more naira when converting export proceeds back to Nigeria
questions.explanation: When naira weakens (depreciates) against the dollar, each dollar converts to more naira, so exporters invoicing in dollars receive more naira. The dollar did not fall in this scenario; exchange rates do affect exporters, and export duties are unrelated to exchange rate movements.

questions.q: A retailer in Ibadan buys goods from a wholesaler at N18, sells at N30. What is the retailer's mark-up on cost expressed as a percentage? (Show working.)
questions.explanation: Mark-up on cost = (Selling price − Cost) ÷ Cost × 100 = (30 − 18) ÷ 18 × 100 = 12 ÷ 18 × 100 = 66.67%. The wrong choices use incorrect denominators or wrong arithmetic; the 40% and 60% figures come from misplacing cost or price in the divisor.

questions.q: Which practice is a wholesale trader most likely to perform that a typical small retail shop does not?
options: Using a shopfront to sell single consumer units to walk-in customers
Carrying out window display merchandising for impulse buyers
Providing credit sales to final consumers on small items
Breaking bulk and offering quantity discounts to retailers
questions.explanation: Wholesalers typically break bulk (sell in smaller lots) and give quantity discounts to retailers, while retail shops sell single consumer units, offer credit to final consumers, and use window displays — activities associated with retail trade rather than wholesale.

questions.q: A freight company in Port Harcourt charges N2,400 per tonne by road and N1,200 per tonne by water. For a shipment of 6 tonnes, what is the savings if the shipper chooses water transport instead of road?
options: N1,200 (difference per tonne only)
questions.explanation: Saving per tonne = 2,400 − 1,200 = 1,200; total saving = 1,200 × 6 = N7,200. N14,400 is the total road cost, not the saving; N1,200 is the per-tonne saving only; N8,400 uses an incorrect per-tonne difference.

questions.q: Which communication channel would be best for a bank in Abuja to send short urgent alerts (account debits, fraud warnings) to thousands of customers quickly?
options: A radio advert aired once each week
A monthly company magazine distributed in branches
Full printed account statements mailed to customers
SMS (short message service) messages to customers' mobile phones
questions.explanation: SMS delivers short, urgent messages quickly and directly to many customers' mobile phones. Printed statements and monthly magazines are slow and not suitable for urgent notices; a weekly radio advert is public and not direct to individual account holders.

questions.q: Ayo bought a smartphone in Lagos with a one-year manufacturer's warranty. After eight months the phone developed a fault unrelated to physical damage. Under Nigerian consumer protection principles, which action is Ayo most entitled to demand from the manufacturer?
options: Be given store credit for the original purchase price instead of repair or replacement
Receive an immediate full refund regardless of whether the fault can be repaired
Receive a refund only if the retailer agrees, since manufacturers don't deal with consumers
Repair the phone free of charge within a reasonable time or replace it if repair is not possible
questions.explanation: A manufacturer's warranty obliges the manufacturer to repair or replace defective goods within the warranty period. A full refund is not automatic unless repair/replacement is impossible or terms specify it. The manufacturer is directly responsible under the warranty, so requiring retailer consent is incorrect.

questions.q: Mrs. Sule bought 10 bottles of a soft drink advertised as 'sugar-free' but discovered it contained sugar. Which regulation or right most directly protects her against this practice?
options: Right to trade secrets protection for the manufacturer
Right to accurate information under consumer protection laws prohibiting false advertising
Right to barter the product for another item without recourse to law
Right to claim punitive damages without proving loss
questions.explanation: Consumer protection laws grant the right to accurate information and prohibit misleading advertisements. Trade secrets protect manufacturers, not consumers. Barter is irrelevant, and punitive damages require legal processes and proof of loss or wilful deception.

questions.q: Which document issued by a carrier serves as evidence of the contract of carriage and often acts as a document of title to goods being shipped abroad?
options: Certificate of origin
Commercial invoice
Pro forma invoice
Bill of lading
questions.explanation: A bill of lading is the carrier's document evidencing the contract of carriage and can act as title to the goods. A commercial invoice details sale terms, pro forma is a preliminary quote, and certificate of origin only states where goods were produced.

questions.q: A Lagos importer receives an insurance certificate covering a shipment. Which single feature distinguishes an insurance certificate from an insurance policy?
options: The certificate is issued by the insured while the policy is issued by customs
The certificate is proof that insurance has been effected; the policy is the full contract of insurance
The certificate lists the premium rate while the policy never shows premiums
The certificate contains legal liabilities while the policy contains only descriptions
questions.explanation: An insurance certificate is evidence that cover exists; the policy is the detailed contract. Premiums appear in the policy or documentation, not exclusively the certificate. The certificate is issued by insurer or broker, not the insured or customs.

questions.q: Chidera pays an annual life insurance premium of N60,000 for a policy with sum assured N3,000,000. She dies in the sixth year after paying premiums for six years. Which principle of life insurance ensures beneficiaries receive the sum assured?
options: Subrogation
Contribution principle
Indemnity principle
Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei)
questions.explanation: Life insurance relies on utmost good faith: applicants must disclose material facts and insurer pays based on contract. Indemnity applies to contracts restoring to prior position (not life insurance). Contribution and subrogation apply to indemnity insurance, not life policies.

questions.q: If the Central Bank of Nigeria increases the monetary policy rate (MPR), which immediate effect is most likely on commercial banks' lending behaviour?
options: Banks increase lending rates, reducing demand for loans
Banks keep lending rates unchanged and increase credit supply
Banks lower lending rates to attract more borrowers
Banks stop taking deposits from the public
questions.explanation: An increase in MPR raises banks' cost of funds, so they typically raise lending rates which reduces loan demand. Lowering rates contradicts higher central bank rates. Banks do not immediately stop deposits or increase credit supply when policy rate rises.

questions.q: Which action by a seller in Abuja would most likely be considered an unfair trade practice under consumer protection laws?
options: Refusing to accept a genuine refund request within the seller's published returns policy
Providing a loyalty card that gives repeat customers benefits
Posting clear terms and conditions about delivery times
Offering a discount to customers who pay in cash
questions.explanation: Refusing to honour the seller's own returns policy is unfair and misleading. Discounts, loyalty schemes, and clear terms are legitimate business practices and not unfair unless deceptive.

questions.q: Which document would an exporter in Port Harcourt present to his bank to obtain payment under a clean collection for shipped goods?
options: Employee payslip of the exporter
Bill of exchange accompanied by shipping documents (e.g., transport document and commercial invoice)
Certificate of incorporation of the buyer
Insurance proposal form only
questions.explanation: Under collection, the exporter presents a bill of exchange and related shipping documents to the bank to collect payment. Insurance proposals, payslips, or buyer's incorporation certificate are irrelevant to payment collection.

questions.q: Mrs. Adeoye wants to start selling handcrafted bags online to customers in Lagos and Abuja. Which e-commerce model best describes her business if she sells directly to final consumers through her own website?
options: Business-to-Business (B2B)
Business-to-Consumer (B2C)
Government-to-Business (G2B)
Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C)
questions.explanation: Selling directly from Mrs. Adeoye's website to final consumers is the B2C model. B2B would involve selling to other businesses, C2C involves transactions between consumers, and G2B involves government sales or services to businesses.

questions.q: A small online retailer in Enugu uses a third-party payment gateway that charges 2.5% per transaction plus a flat N50. For a sale of N10,000 what total fee will the retailer pay to the gateway?
questions.explanation: 2.5% of N10,000 is N250; adding the flat N50 gives N300. N250 omits the flat fee, N275 would be 2.75%, and N350 would be 3.5% plus the flat fee.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best measure to protect customer data on an e-commerce site in Nigeria?
options: Publish data privacy policy but do not implement technical controls
Rely only on passwords without encryption
Keep customer data on a public cloud without access controls
Use HTTPS, strong encryption for stored data and enforce multi-factor authentication
questions.explanation: Combining HTTPS, encryption and multi-factor authentication provides technical protection for data. Relying only on passwords or public cloud without controls leaves data vulnerable; a policy without technical measures is insufficient.

questions.q: Which form of business unit has the advantage of limited liability for owners and can sell shares to the public in Nigeria?
options: Cooperative society
Sole proprietorship
Public limited company
Partnership
questions.explanation: A public limited company offers limited liability and may sell shares to the public. Sole proprietorships and partnerships typically involve unlimited liability; cooperatives are owned by members and are not primarily for public share trading.

questions.q: Chinelo sets up a small bakery in Owerri and hires family members to help. She keeps personal and business receipts in the same notebook and pays business bills from her personal account. Which accounting principle is she failing to observe?
options: Business entity (separate entity) principle
Consistency principle
Going concern principle
Matching principle
questions.explanation: Mixing personal and business transactions violates the business entity principle which requires separation of owner and business records. Going concern concerns longevity, consistency is about methods, and matching relates expenses with revenues.

questions.q: A cooperative society in Kaduna issues surplus to members based on their purchases during the year. This surplus distribution is known as:
options: Interest
Dividend or patronage refund
Capital gain
Brokerage
questions.explanation: Cooperatives distribute surplus to members as dividends or patronage refunds based on use. Brokerage relates to agents, interest is on loans, and capital gain arises from selling assets at a profit.

questions.q: Mr. Bello plans to invest in shares listed on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX). Which document shows the ownership of a share and is usually required to trade in the secondary market?
options: Transport waybill
Share certificate or electronic statement of holdings
Export licence
Trademark certificate
questions.explanation: Ownership is evidenced by a share certificate or electronic statement of holdings. Trademark certificates, export licences, and waybills are unrelated to share ownership.

questions.q: A stock on the NGX is quoted at N8.50 per share. An investor buys 1,000 shares and pays a brokerage fee of 1% of the transaction value. What is the total cost to the investor?
questions.explanation: Transaction value = 1,000 × N8.50 = N8,500. Brokerage = 1% of N8,500 = N85. Total cost = N8,500 + N85 = N8,585. N8,500 omits brokerage; N8,600 and N8,590 are incorrect calculations.

questions.q: In an agricultural community near Ilorin, most households engage in subsistence farming to feed their families and sell small surpluses. This type of occupation is best described as:
options: Primary occupation with subsistence production
Quaternary occupation with information services
Tertiary occupation with commercial production
Secondary occupation with industrial production
questions.explanation: Subsistence farming is a primary occupation involving production of raw agricultural goods mainly for family consumption. Tertiary refers to services, secondary to manufacturing, and quaternary to knowledge-based services.

questions.q: Mrs. Okafor in Onitsha bought a sewing machine advertised as 'new' but it failed within two weeks and the seller said it was 'as-is'. Under Nigerian consumer protection principles, which remedy is Mrs. Okafor most likely entitled to from the seller?
options: Full refund or repair because the product was misrepresented as new
A minor price reduction only because it was sold 'as-is'
No remedy because the buyer accepted the machine at purchase
Only a replacement if the manufacturer agrees to a warranty claim
questions.explanation: Misrepresenting a product as 'new' when it is not is an unfair practice; the buyer can demand a full refund or repair. The 'as-is' claim by a seller does not override statutory protection against misrepresentation, so a mere price reduction or no remedy is not appropriate.

questions.q: A Lagos supermarket labels a soft drink 'sugar-free' but tests show it contains sugar. Which action by the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) is most appropriate?
options: Treat the matter as civil only and refuse to take any enforcement action
Seize the supermarket's entire business licence permanently without investigation
Require corrective advertising, order product withdrawal and impose penalties
Ignore it because only manufacturers, not retailers, can be sanctioned
questions.explanation: When a product is falsely labelled, the regulator can require corrective advertising, order withdrawal of the product and impose penalties. Permanent licence seizure without due process is excessive; enforcement is not limited to manufacturers because retailers may be liable for selling false-labelled items.

questions.q: Which function best describes a bill of lading issued by a carrier to an exporter in Port Harcourt?
options: A customs declaration used to assess import duty
An insurance policy covering loss at sea
A commercial invoice used to request payment from the buyer
Evidence of the contract of carriage and document of title to the goods
questions.explanation: A bill of lading serves both as evidence of the contract of carriage and as a document of title. It is not an insurance policy, customs declaration, or commercial invoice, though those documents are used in international trade.

questions.q: An exporter prefers the greatest certainty of payment for an overseas shipment. Which payment method gives the exporter the strongest assurance that payment will be made by the buyer's bank?
options: Open account transaction
Confirmed irrevocable letter of credit
Consignment sale
Revocable letter of credit
questions.explanation: A confirmed irrevocable letter of credit guarantees payment by the buyer's bank and the confirming bank, providing the highest assurance. A revocable LC can be altered or cancelled; open account and consignment leave the exporter exposed to buyer default.

questions.q: Chidera pays an annual life assurance premium of N60,000 for a policy with a sum assured of N3,000,000. What is the premium rate as a percentage of the sum assured?
questions.explanation: Rate = (premium ÷ sum assured) × 100 = (60,000 ÷ 3,000,000) × 100 = 0.02 × 100 = 2%. 0.5% or 1% are too low and 20% is far too high.

questions.q: If the Central Bank of Nigeria raises the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR), which is the most likely immediate response by commercial banks?
options: Cease accepting deposits from new customers
Reduce the statutory reserve requirement for deposits
Increase their lending (loan) interest rates
Lower lending rates to attract more borrowers
questions.explanation: When the central bank raises the MPR, commercial banks typically raise their lending rates to reflect the higher cost of funds. Changing reserve requirements or ceasing to accept deposits are not the usual immediate responses, and lowering lending rates would contradict the higher policy rate.
